cards.title: Clavicle

fields.Function: Connects the shoulder girdle to the sternum.

objectives: Identify Clavicle and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Scapula

fields.Function: Provides the glenoid and shoulder muscle attachments.

objectives: Identify Scapula and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Deltoid

fields.Attachments: Clavicle, acromion and scapular spine to deltoid tuberosity.
fields.Clinical relevance: Weak abduction may prompt assessment of axillary nerve function; it is not specific to a single lesion.

objectives: Identify Deltoid and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Supraspinatus

fields.Function: Initiates abduction and supports joint stability.

objectives: Identify Supraspinatus and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Infraspinatus
objectives: Identify Infraspinatus and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Teres minor

fields.Relations: A rotator cuff component; distinguish it from teres major.

objectives: Identify Teres minor and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Subscapularis
objectives: Identify Subscapularis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Teres major

fields.Function: Adducts and medially rotates the arm.
fields.Relations: Inferior to teres minor; not a rotator cuff component.

objectives: Identify Teres major and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Humerus

fields.Relations: Head meets the scapula; distal end meets radius and ulna.

objectives: Identify Humerus and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Biceps brachii

fields.Function: Flexes the elbow; supinates the forearm.

objectives: Identify Biceps brachii and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Brachialis

fields.Innervation: Predominantly musculocutaneous nerve; the lateral portion may receive radial supply.

objectives: Identify Brachialis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Coracobrachialis

fields.Relations: The nerve usually passes through the muscle.

objectives: Identify Coracobrachialis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Triceps brachii
objectives: Identify Triceps brachii and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Brachioradialis
objectives: Identify Brachioradialis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Brachial artery

fields.Function: Main arterial conduit through the arm.

objectives: Identify Brachial artery and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Radius

fields.Function: Lateral forearm bone in anatomical position.
fields.Relations: Thumb-side bone; its distal end articulates with scaphoid and lunate.

objectives: Identify Radius and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Ulna

fields.Function: Medial forearm bone in anatomical position.
fields.Relations: Olecranon forms the bony prominence at the elbow.

objectives: Identify Ulna and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Pronator teres
objectives: Identify Pronator teres and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Pronator quadratus

fields.Innervation: Anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve.

objectives: Identify Pronator quadratus and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Supinator

fields.Innervation: Deep branch of the radial nerve.

objectives: Identify Supinator and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Flexor carpi radialis
objectives: Identify Flexor carpi radialis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Flexor carpi ulnaris
objectives: Identify Flexor carpi ulnaris and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Palmaris longus
objectives: Identify Palmaris longus and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Flexor digitorum superficialis
objectives: Identify Flexor digitorum superficialis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Flexor digitorum profundus

fields.Innervation: Lateral part: anterior interosseous nerve. Medial part: ulnar nerve.

objectives: Identify Flexor digitorum profundus and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Flexor pollicis longus

fields.Innervation: Anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve.

objectives: Identify Flexor pollicis longus and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Extensor carpi radialis longus
objectives: Identify Extensor carpi radialis longus and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Extensor carpi radialis brevis

fields.Innervation: Deep branch of the radial nerve.

objectives: Identify Extensor carpi radialis brevis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Extensor digitorum
objectives: Identify Extensor digitorum and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Extensor carpi ulnaris
objectives: Identify Extensor carpi ulnaris and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Radial artery

fields.Function: Arterial pathway on the radial side.

objectives: Identify Radial artery and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Ulnar artery

fields.Function: Arterial pathway on the ulnar side.

objectives: Identify Ulnar artery and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Scaphoid

fields.Function: Radial bone of the proximal carpal row.

objectives: Identify Scaphoid and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Lunate

fields.Function: Proximal carpal bone articulating with the radius.

objectives: Identify Lunate and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Flexor retinaculum

fields.Function: Forms the roof of the carpal tunnel.
fields.Relations: The median nerve traverses the tunnel beneath it.
fields.Clinical relevance: Tunnel compression can affect median nerve function.

objectives: Identify Flexor retinaculum and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Abductor pollicis brevis

fields.Innervation: Recurrent branch of the median nerve.

objectives: Identify Abductor pollicis brevis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Opponens pollicis

fields.Innervation: Recurrent branch of the median nerve.

objectives: Identify Opponens pollicis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Adductor pollicis

fields.Innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

objectives: Identify Adductor pollicis and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Extensor pollicis longus
objectives: Identify Extensor pollicis longus and explain its regional relationships.

cards.title: Abductor pollicis longus

fields.Function: Abducts the thumb at its base.

objectives: Identify Abductor pollicis longus and explain its regional relationships.

questions.explanation: The deltoid receives axillary nerve supply.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which humeral region is closely related to the axillary nerve?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve passes around the surgical neck.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which cuff muscle initiates arm abduction?
questions.explanation: Supraspinatus contributes to the initiation of abduction.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.explanation: Teres minor receives axillary nerve supply.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.explanation: Biceps receives musculocutaneous nerve supply.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is deep to biceps and assists elbow flexion?
questions.explanation: Brachialis lies beneath biceps.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.explanation: Radial nerve supply supports triceps function.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which action is most directly associated with triceps?
questions.explanation: Triceps extends the elbow.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which muscle flexes the thumb interphalangeal joint?
questions.explanation: Flexor pollicis longus acts on the thumb interphalangeal joint.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which nerve branch supplies this muscle?
questions.explanation: This median nerve branch supplies flexor pollicis longus.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies flexor carpi ulnaris?
questions.explanation: Flexor carpi ulnaris receives ulnar supply.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies flexor carpi radialis?
questions.explanation: Flexor carpi radialis receives median supply.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which structure forms the tunnel roof?
questions.explanation: The flexor retinaculum spans the palmar carpal arch.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which nerve passes through the carpal tunnel?
questions.explanation: The median nerve passes through the tunnel beneath the retinaculum.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is associated with thumb opposition?
questions.explanation: Opponens pollicis supports opposition.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

questions.explanation: Adductor pollicis receives deep ulnar branch supply.
objectives: Apply regional anatomy to a clinical teaching scenario.

cases.title: Shoulder weakness after injury
cases.presentation: After shoulder trauma, a student is asked to explain reduced deltoid function. These prompts test anatomical relationships, not diagnosis.
objectives: Explain anatomical relationships in shoulder weakness after injury.

cases.title: Explaining rotator cuff movement
cases.presentation: A tutor asks you to connect a movement deficit with a rotator cuff muscle.
objectives: Explain anatomical relationships in explaining rotator cuff movement.

cases.title: Weak elbow flexion
cases.presentation: During an anatomy discussion, a student compares the motor supply of anterior arm muscles.
objectives: Explain anatomical relationships in weak elbow flexion.

cases.title: Posterior arm and nerve function
cases.presentation: A teaching case asks you to distinguish the nerve supply of posterior arm muscles from anterior arm muscles.
objectives: Explain anatomical relationships in posterior arm and nerve function.

cases.title: The precision pinch discussion
cases.presentation: A tutor asks you to explain the anatomical basis of thumb-tip flexion during a precision pinch.
objectives: Explain anatomical relationships in the precision pinch discussion.

cases.title: Two wrist flexors, different nerves
cases.presentation: Compare the nerve supply of the radial and ulnar wrist flexors.
objectives: Explain anatomical relationships in two wrist flexors, different nerves.

cases.title: Anatomy of carpal tunnel compression
cases.presentation: A wrist-compression teaching scenario asks you to identify the tunnel roof and the nerve within it.
objectives: Explain anatomical relationships in anatomy of carpal tunnel compression.

cases.title: Thumb opposition versus adduction
cases.presentation: A student distinguishes two thumb actions and their motor pathways.
objectives: Explain anatomical relationships in thumb opposition versus adduction.

objectives: Relate nerve supply to selected muscles.

objectives: Relate nerve supply to selected muscles.

nerves.title: Median nerve
nerves.description: Selected muscles receive supply from the median nerve or its branches. The mixed supply of profundus is described separately.
objectives: Relate nerve supply to selected muscles.

nerves.title: Ulnar nerve
nerves.description: Selected examples of ulnar motor supply. This map does not include every muscle or sensory territory.
objectives: Relate nerve supply to selected muscles.
